articleHeadline: River Confluence Microbes Show Complex Genomic Potential During Mass
articleSummary: At the Sangam confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna in Prayagraj, India, the Mahakumbh pilgrimage triggers episodic perturbations of river microbiota, with major inputs of organic matter, nutrients, pharmaceuticals, personal-care products, fecal material, and skin microbes from upstream runoff. 16S rRNA sequencing shows baseline dominance of Proteobacteria, Firmicutes, Actinobacteria, and Bacteroidetes, including Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter, Bacillus, Aeromonas, and Streptomyces; during mass bathing, blooms of Escherichia, Klebsiella, and Vibrio appear, with metal-tolerant taxa rising. Pre-event BOD is 2.37 mg/L, rising to ~6.37 mg/L during the festival and about 4.93 mg/L post-event; earlier festivals reported BOD 14 mg/L, COD 67 mg/L, ammonium 2.15 mg/L, and a ~130-fold biomass increase with 792 and 482 MPN/100 mL for total and fecal coliforms. COD peaks near 30 mg/L; pH shifts from 8.17 to 8.53, then 8.33; DO declines with respiration. The review defines genomic resilience as a population’s capacity to maintain or recover function after disturbance via genetic or regulatory changes, and distinguishes it from resistance, acclimation, and adaptation. An observational ecogenomic framework is proposed, noting many taxa are freshwater natives and source attribution remains unresolved.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Are hepatitis B and C co-infections dangerous?

articleSummary: Co-infection with hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) means simultaneous infection with both pathogens. Transmission is mainly via blood (shared needles or non-sterile equipment); HBV also via sexual contact and mother-to-child, while HCV is less often sexual but possible. The dual infection often accelerates liver disease; viruses can interact, with reactivation of one driving damage by the other. Co-infected individuals have faster progression to fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma, and risk of ascites, esophageal variceal bleeding, hepatic encephalopathy, or liver failure. Evaluation includes HBV DNA, HCV RNA, liver enzymes, coagulation, and bilirubin; therapy is personalized. DAAs can cure most HCV; HBV treatment depends on DNA level, enzymes, and fibrosis stage. Seek medical assessment early; do not stop HBV meds or self-treat HCV. Limit alcohol, avoid hepatotoxic products, and monitor for liver cancer if cirrhosis risk persists. By Dr. Mai Hoai Sang, Ho Chi Minh City hospital.

articleSummary: H9N2 avian influenza: ginsenoside Rg1 adjuvant enhances vaccine protection in chickens. articleSummary: Late-2025 records in Corguinho, Mato Grosso do Sul, show 19 positive cases of tegumentary (cutaneous) leishmaniasis; visceral leishmaniasis (kalazar) has not been detected there. Tegumentary disease causes skin lesions, sometimes mucosal ulcers; visceral leishmaniasis targets internal organs (spleen, liver, bone marrow) and can be fatal without treatment. Incubation typically 2–3 months (range two weeks to two years). In 2025, MS registered 125 new tegumentary cases with 11 relapses; nationwide 9,984 new cases and 741 relapses (MS: 146 cures, 1 death, 5 abandonments). Visceral leishmaniasis in MS had 38 new cases and 4 relapses with 8 deaths (9.88% fatality); Brazil: 1,331 new, 196 relapses, 125 deaths. Diagnosis combines clinical assessment with parasitological tests; treatment is free via SUS, started sometimes on clinical grounds.

articleHeadline: Childhood Infections in Beijing Show Divergent Age and Seasonal Shifts
articleSummary: Pertussis shows the most dramatic rebound after relaxation of COVID-19 measures in Haidian District, Beijing, with overall incidence increasing nearly tenfold (IRR 9.93; 95% CI 4.82–20.44). In 2023 there were 104 pertussis cases and 187 in 2024 among children aged 6–14 years, a group with zero cases in the 2015–2019 baseline. Hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) overall declined (IRR 0.49; 95% CI 0.35–0.69), though time-trend adjustment attenuates significance; HFMD shifted toward older ages with under-6 incidence falling (IRR 0.37) and 10–14-year-olds rising (272.6 per 100,000). Median age increased from 3.55 to 6.33 years, and the school-age to preschool incidence ratio rose 3.59-fold (95% CI 2.06–6.28). HFMD seasonality also shifted, with the circular mean peak moving from late July to late September (P<0.001). Mumps declined in preschool and school-age groups (IRRs ~0.37–0.39); no major shifts in seasonality. Findings derive from 23,379 Beijing Haidian records (2015–2025), underscoring demographic and timing changes beyond case counts.

There are twelve serogroups; A, B, C, W, X and Y account for about 95% of cases.
